title: EU Parliament Fails to Block Chat Control 1.0 on 9 July 2026 — Breyer: "Our Children Lose Out"
summary: The European Parliament failed to block the revival of Chat Control 1.0 on 9 July 2026, with 314 MEPs voting to reject against 276 to keep — falling short of the 361 absolute majority required. Patrick Breyer quoted the outcome as 'Our children lose out.' Pitched from Breyer's advocacy site as the primary source.
body: Editor's note. This draft, filed under THE-1088, covered the European Parliament's 9 July 2026 fail-to-block vote on Chat Control 1.0 — the interim ePrivacy derogation that permits platforms to voluntarily scan private messages for child sexual abuse material. The Source Checker passed a verified brief at confidence 0.9, corroborated by The Register, Heise, Euronews, EU Perspectives, Brussels Signal, and TechTimes. The primary pitch source was Patrick Breyer's advocacy page (patrick-breyer.de), which quoted him: 'Our children lose out.' Before drafting, a pre-submission catalog check against the live issue index returned a determinative match: THE-1040 ('Parliament Voted Against Chat Control. It Passed Anyway.', Sable Ren, confidence 0.86) is already published at slug chat-control-1-0-survives-parliament-9-jul-vote. THE-1040 covers the identical event — the same vote, the same tally (314 against / 276 for / 17 abstentions), the same absolute-majority threshold of 361, and the same 2028 derogation end-date. The Breyer-advocacy source material offers no distinct angle: Breyer's quotes and the false-positive statistics attributed to him were available context at the time of THE-1040's reporting and do not constitute a new story on a separate news event. This is also at minimum the third pipeline run on this event (see THE-1032, cancelled as a duplicate of THE-1040; THE-1039, cancelled at draft stage; the Breyer URL itself flagged for recirculation in THE-867). The reporter withdrew before drafting. The canonical Signal Noise record for this story is the published piece at chat-control-1-0-survives-parliament-9-jul-vote.
